name: tally
description: Personal finance web app for accounts, credit card bills and instalments. React, TypeScript, Supabase, PWA.

paragraphs: A personal finance app for tracking accounts, credit card bills and upcoming payments, built around how money actually moves in Brazil.
Live demo (sample data kept in your browser, no sign-up)

Money in Brazil runs on the credit card: purchases split into instalments, bills that close on one day and fall due on another, and fixed monthly expenses. The finance app I used handled this but charged a monthly fee and didn't quite fit how I work, so I built my own. The biggest change: money I put into savings disappears from every total, so the balance I see is the money I can actually spend. It runs on desktop and installs on a phone's home screen.
features: Accounts and credit cards, each card with its limit, closing day and due day; purchases land on the right bill automatically
Fixed (recurring) entries and instalment purchases, shown as "2/4" on each bill
Two views of the same month: Cash flow shows each unpaid card bill as one expense on its due date, All transactions shows every purchase instead
Pay a card bill in full or in part, from any account
Savings accounts kept out of the balance, income and expense totals, with a toggle to show the amount saved

whatItDoes.text: A personal finance app for tracking accounts, credit card bills and upcoming payments, built around how money actually moves in Brazil.

requirements.text: One transactions table holds expenses, income, transfers and bill payments, and check constraints spell out what each kind must have: an expense comes from an account or a card but never both, a transfer needs a destination account, a bill payment needs an account and a card, and only card entries carry a bill month.

An approximate converted total is optional and off by default: it fetches the European Central Bank's daily rates from Frankfurter, which needs no API key, caches them for hours, and nothing stored ever depends on them.
Run npm run dev and create an account at /criar-conta.
